revisions.text: Pause before answering an insult, then choose a fair response; fairness may require a firm objection.

content.text: Pause before answering an insult, then choose a fair response; fairness may require a firm objection.

revisions.scope: Responding to an insult when some response is called for.
revisions.qualifications: Calm does not require passive acceptance of injustice.
revisions.assumptions: A pause can create room to reconsider the next response.
revisions.practical_implication: Pause before replying, reconsider your judgment, and choose a fair response—including a firm objection when appropriate.

revisions.text: Let the first surge pass. Then respond fairly—even when fairness calls for a firm objection.

content.text: Let the first surge pass. Then respond fairly—even when fairness calls for a firm objection.

revisions.text: If you do this, you will never feel anger again.

content.text: If you do this, you will never feel anger again.

revisions.assumptions: Unsupported universal prediction: none of the fixture passages promises freedom from anger.

bundles.explanation: A.1 proposes a pause; B.2 supplies the standard of fairness; C.3 limits any inference that calm requires submission. They jointly support this conditional teaching; none alone establishes the whole statement.

links.justification: The pause is an opportunity to examine the added judgment.
The next response should be fair, when a response is required.
A firm objection may be consistent with calm.

c1:r1.notes: Synthetic proposal. Review each link, then the joint inference.

e2:r1.notes: The sources do not promise that anger will never return.
